Hi all — I pulled the usage window Nov 1–7 for StellarScout. Summary below; I've attached a fuller CSV and a small JSON with sampled request payloads.

Short summary (UTC) Nov 1: we recorded a ~98,700 token increase attributed to model-redwood/gptx-3.2-gen (generation) across ~1,100 requests. Embeddings-only endpoints (model-redwood/emb-small) show ~12k tokens for the same window.

Preliminary observations:
- Several requests to /v1/chat/stream included both a system prompt and a large user-provided context that appears to have been repeated across calls (prefix caching won't compress across distinct request_ids).
- We see a small cluster of replayed request_ids (6 unique request_ids repeated 3–4x) originating from the eu-west-1 edge between 02:10–02:17 UTC. Those repeats account for ~22k of the spike.
- One agent reported switching from embedding endpoint to chat/generative endpoint in a deployment rollout on Nov 1 — this would change token classification from embedding units to generation tokens.

Files attached: usage_snapshot_2027-11-01.csv (full rows), sample_request_logs_20271101.json (3 sampled request payloads).

Next steps I propose:
1) Provide the repeated request_ids and the timestamped logs (we have included samples).
2) If StellarScout can confirm the agent rollout (embed->gen), we can mark those as correctly billed.
3) If the repeats are accidental (replay/batch retry), we can offer a provisional credit for the duplicated requests while you investigate.

I'll hold on the provisional credit until we have confirmation of which of the repeated request_ids you want us to waive.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
